title: RAMALC collectives expansion pass 9
summary: Expanded the current RAMALC collective directory into seven organization nodes, seven recursive investigation targets, three public people and ten typed organization/person relations while preserving unresolved operational status for directory-listed collectives lacking independent current activity evidence.

provenance.method: bounded breadth-first first-party network expansion with current-status re-verification and repository deduplication

classification_rules: Treat RAMALC's current first-party directory as explicit evidence that a named organization is publicly listed as a RAMALC collective.
Do not equate current directory listing with independently verified current operational activity; retain operational-status uncertainty where separate current evidence was not found.
Treat current first-party organization activity as sufficient to mark ACOOC, Laboratorio de Paz, Colectivo CASA and SERPAJ Paraguay active-current.
Store Angela Cuenca's 2024 first-party representation as historical-recent with current role unresolved rather than silently promoting it to a current role.
data.method: Start from the merged RAMALC regional-network seed, enumerate every collective visible on its current first-party directory, re-check operational status with current public surfaces, cross-enumerate public people where strong evidence exists, and queue each distinct collective for further graph expansion.
data.narrative_role: bounded chapter/affiliate and public-person expansion investigator
data.research_question: Which public RAMALC collectives and public-person edges can be materialized from the current network directory in this bounded pass?

findings.finding: RAMALC's current first-party network page exposes seven named collectives across Colombia, Paraguay, Venezuela and Bolivia.
ACOOC, Laboratorio de Paz, Colectivo CASA and SERPAJ Paraguay each have independently observable current public activity surfaces in addition to the RAMALC directory listing.

Rafael Uzcátegui is explicitly identified as current co-director of Laboratorio de Paz; Lexys Rendón is publicly listed on the organization's first-party team page; Angela Cuenca is retained as a 2024 public Colectivo CASA representative with current role unresolved.
